title: VehicleWheel3D suspension force calculation is wrong, and N/mm unit is misleading
body: ### Tested versions Godot v4.5.stable.mono ### System information Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8157) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-11800H @ 2.30GHz (16 threads) - 15.75 GiB memory ### Issue description Currently, the stiffness of the VehicleWheel3D node is stored as N/mm unit, however inside [vehicle_body_3d.cpp](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/cb3af5afff15669a684ba4f04b9aa5c70dfd09ad/scene/3d/physics/vehicle_body_3d.cpp#L559), this value is multiplied by spring offset (unit meters) without any unit conversion. Then later, the force value is multiplied by the vehicle mass, which makes no sense. When people use the vehiclewheel3d and see the stiffness as a unit of Newtons per length (mm), they expect it to follow Hooke's Law, which is F=kx, where k is stiffness in terms of N/m, and x is the spring offset in terms of m. There should be no vehicle mass in this equation My proposed change is to remove the mass multiplication, and add "*1000.0" into the formula as a conversion from N/mm to N/m. This would accurately reflect the unit N/mm displayed to the users. Pseudocode: ``` force = wheel_info.m_suspensionStiffness * 1000.0 * length_diff * wheel_info.m_clippedInvContactDotSuspension; ... // RESULT wheel_info.m_wheelsSuspensionForce = force; ``` The suspension length is also calculated wrong, which is solved by this PR [112440](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112440) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new 3D project in Godot v4.5.stable.mono. 2. Add a VehicleBody3D with mass 400kg node to the scene. (so weight is 400*9.8=3920N). 3. Add 4 VehicleWheel3D node as a child of the VehicleBody3D. (so we expect each wheel holds 3920/4=980N). Use stiffness=16N/mm; suspension_travel=spring_rest_length=0.5m, wheel_radius=0.5m 5. While the project is running, once the vehicle is stable, change the mass of the vehicle up and down. Notice how the vehicle does not move. This indicate the force strength increase or decrease depends on the chassis mass which does not reflect the N/mm unit. 6. For the same suspension properties, a heavier vehicle is expected to compress more than a lighter vehicle, but it is not the case for the current implementation. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
